units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 2:3:7">Y. Maasr. II, 49ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>חצר בית ש׳</he> a well-guarded court (= <he>חצר המשתמרת</he>, v. <cite ref="H01544"><he>חָצֵר</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:6:3">Y. Sabb. II, 5ᵇ</cite> top <he>אינו צריך ש׳</he> (omit <he>ליה</he>) is not in need of special guard (against dangers).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 42a:7">B. Mets. 42ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 31b:9">Pes. 31ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="K00953"><he>כֶּסֶף</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:1">B. Kam. I, 1</cite> <he>שְׁמִירָתָן עליך</he> thou art bound to guard them.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>כל שחבתי בשְׁמִירָתוֹ</he>, v. <cite ref="H00231"><he>חוּב</he></cite> h.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 4a:17">Ib. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>אדם שְׁמִירת גופו עליו הוא</he> a human being is his own guard (the employer has no responsibility for injury done by the employee).—
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 4">Num. R. s. 4<sup>4</sup></cite> <he>יש פקידה לש׳</he> trust (the root <he>פקד</he>) is used in the sense of guarding (taking charge).

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 25">Ex. R. s. 25</cite>, end <he>על שמירת יום וכ׳</he> the son of David comes as a reward for the observance of one Sabbath day; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="U01484"><he>שְׁמִירוֹת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 816:2">Yalk. Ps. 816</cite> (ref. to <he>שמרות</he>, <cite ref="Psalms 77:5">Ps. LXXVII, 5</cite>) <he>כל שְׁמִירוֹתַי בלילה</he> all my watchings (waiting for help) are held by night; Midr. Till. to Ps. l. c. <cite ref="U01534"><he>שמרותי</he></cite> (ed. Bub. <he>מידותי</he>, corr. acc.).
